Indian Standard
GUIDELINES FOR GRADING OF RAW HIDES AND SKINS
0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 6 June 1979, after the draft finalized by the Leather Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 Considering the requests from the tanning industry to develop some prompt and easy method of assessing the quality of raw hides and skins, the Leather Sectional Committee decided to formulate this Indian It is expected that this would be found useful by tanners and Standard. raw hide and skib purchasers and selectors. 0.3 The quality of raw hides and skins may differ considerably due to various influencing factors, namely, breed, feeding, living conditions,.sex, age and health of the animals, substance ( thickness of the hide or skin ), appearance of hair, various grain defects, flaying, curing, storage, and transportation of the hides and skins. The selection is generally based on the area or weight, substance, surface defects on grain and flesh sides and general appearance of the hide/skin. It, is well recognized that no single test method is capable of evaluatingYaw cured stock and even today the most accepted method in different. parts of the world is to examine the hides visually and by physical handling.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes guidelines for ready assessment of raw hides and skins by visual evaluation applicable to bovine hides, calf skins and goat and sheep skins. 1.1.1 This standard hides and skins. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 nor the purpose shall apply. of this standard definitions given in IS : l&&1960+ does not lay down specifications of quality for raw

*Glossary of terms relating to hides, skins and leather. 3

3. EVALUATION 3.1 General - Finished leather quality may be affected by many of the defects prevailing in raw hides and skins but all of them are not visible in the raw or salted stock. Moreover, the damage caused by some of them are minor and the occurrence of some of the defects is rare. defects which are responsible for substantial 3.1 Defects -Those devaluation of finished leather and are recognizable in the raw/salted state should be considered as the criteria for evaluating raw hide/skin quality. 3.2 Classification - Hides and skins in one lot shall be first classified into different categories according to area or mass and then they should be graded for quality for each category according to Table 1.
